subject: Decision Making
title: Embracing Imperfect Decisions
description: A quick, practical guide to Embracing Imperfect Decisions.

hook.text: Jeff Bezos says most decisions should be made with 70 percent of the information you wish you had. Waiting costs more.

buildup.text: Type 1 decisions are irreversible and need caution. Type 2 decisions are reversible and need speed. Most are Type 2.

discovery.text: Treating every decision as Type 1 causes paralysis. Organizations that demand certainty move too slowly to compete.

twist.text: Embracing Imperfect Decisions shows that the best decision is often not the most intuitive one.

climax.text: Under pressure, perfect is the enemy of good enough. Act, learn, and adjust.

punchline.text: Seventy percent and go. Speed of learning beats perfection of planning.

quiz.question: What is Jeff Bezos' rule for most decisions?
options: Decide with about 70% of desired information because waiting costs more than adjusting
